findings.title: Six rules tagged check=["weakness"] are already checked by a panel, contradicting RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK's own bar
locations: catalog/hats/doc-policy.toml:8 — states HOME_ORDER's order, MODULE_MAP's map content, and ONE_HOME/VARIANT_PAIR's f/f! rule almost verbatim
catalog/lanes/check-docs.toml:26 — the 'family' cross-lane explicitly checks ONE_HOME and VARIANT_PAIR
catalog/hats/structure-consistency.toml:6 — restates the HOME_ORDER skeleton as its audit template
catalog/hats/latex-typesetter.toml:9 — lists 'the upright imaginary unit \mathrm{i}' among enforced house-set items
catalog/hats/citations-integrity.toml:6 — checks the clickable-DOI / Open-Library requirement
findings.description: RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK reserves 'weakness' for a rule with no check at all, distinct from 'panel' ('a rule a reading panel decides inside an instrument that runs'). For these six rules a reading panel already does decide them — doc-policy.toml and structure-consistency.toml (check-consistency instrument) state HOME_ORDER's/MODULE_MAP's content almost verbatim, the check-docs 'family' cross-lane exists specifically to check ONE_HOME/VARIANT_PAIR, latex-typesetter.toml names the imaginary-unit rule explicitly, and citations-integrity.toml names the DOI rule explicitly. Left as 'weakness', the rule registry's own debt ledger overstates unchecked debt for six rules that are in fact covered — the registry drift RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK exists to prevent.
findings.resolution_hint: Re-tag these six rules' check field to include "panel" (matching sibling rules like TWO_TIER and LEADING_IDENTITY that already use it for the same doc-policy coverage).

findings.title: RULE.DOC.ALIASING_BULLET is tagged check=["panel"] but no hat or lane names its actual (placement) requirement
locations: catalog/hats/doc-policy.toml:8 — enumerates its enforcement list; no mention of aliasing or the destination bullet
catalog/seeds/fixture.toml:55-59 — the only 'alias' hit in catalog/: the 'false-property' seed negates an aliasing CLAIM's truth (VERIFIED's territory), not its placement
findings.description: RULE.DOC.ALIASING_BULLET's content is structural: the aliasing statement must live in the destination argument's bullet, not as standalone prose. A case-insensitive grep of every file under catalog/ and instruments/ for 'alias' finds only bug-hunt's generic 'aliasing' bug-kind and the seeds fixture's content-truth test — neither checks placement. Unlike its neighbours (ONE_HOME, TWO_TIER, LINKS, NO_DEAD_REFS), which doc-policy.toml names explicitly, no persona or lane brief names ALIASING_BULLET's placement rule, so no panel visibly decides it — the mirror-image of finding 1.
findings.resolution_hint: Add a clause to doc-policy.toml's persona naming the destination-bullet placement rule, or re-tag ALIASING_BULLET's check to "weakness" until one exists.

findings.title: Five testing-protocol rules tagged check=["panel"] have no corresponding hat/lane/workflow reference in the available ground truth
locations: policy/RULES.toml — RULE.TEST.GATE_VS_SURVEY, RULE.TEST.DEFINITION_OF_DONE, RULE.TEST.MUTATION, RULE.TEST.BOTH_DIRECTIONS, RULE.TEST.MISSING_IS_FAILING (all `check = ["panel"]`)

catalog/hats/*.toml, catalog/lanes/*.toml, instruments/*/workflow/*.js — grepped for 'oracle', 'mutation', 'both direction(s)', 'gate...survey', 'definition of done', 'symmetric fixture'; no hit names these rules' substance
findings.description: None of the four instruments' declared objects (changes to code, source prose, rendered prose, the code) is 'the test suite's own construction discipline', and no catalog hat or lane brief in this snapshot names gate-vs-survey placement, mutation-testing discipline, bidirectional-check review, or missing-case-is-failing review. Reported at low confidence because each consumer's own .gbg/config.toml (out of scope here) could in principle add a bug-hunt territory or lanes_extra entry covering this without it appearing in the shared catalog.
findings.resolution_hint: Confirm via the tool's own .gbg/config.toml whether any running instrument's panel actually reads new tests against these five rules; if none does, re-tag them "weakness".
